national_raw_news.title: 42 mins ago | National 63 India scripted successful conservation journey from 523 lions to 891 in last 10 years: PM Modi on...
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 10, 2026 2:31 PM India scripted successful conservation journey from 523 lions to 891 in last 10 years: PM Modi on World Lion Day On the occasion of World Lion Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that India’s Asiatic lion population is thriving, with its habitat and range expanding. Sharing an article written by Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, Mr Modi highlighted that the Government’s unwavering commitment to conservation, backed by strong community participation, is an inspiring example of protecting the country’s wildlife and preserving the species for generations to come. The article written by Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupendra Yadav points out that the lions’ range has expanded from around 30 thousand square kilometres in 2020 to nearly 35 thousand square kilometres, covering 11 districts. It also talks about how India scripted the successful conservation journey of 523 lions in 2015 to 891 in 2025. national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 116 Over ten lakh people evacuated as typhoon Dolphin batters parts of Eastern China
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 10, 2026 2:28 PM Over ten lakh people evacuated as typhoon Dolphin batters parts of Eastern China Chinese authorities have evacuated more than one million people from eastern China, including Shanghai, as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall. The typhoon brought heavy rain and disrupted transport across the region. Nearly 1,000 flights were cancelled in Shanghai today. Authorities have downgraded Dolphin to a tropical storm. China had earlier issued its highest-level red alert for Dolphin, which is the strongest storm to hit the country this year. Dolphin had maximum wind speeds of 150 kilometres per hour when it first struck Yuhuan in Zhejiang province yesterday. Heavy rain has been forecast for Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces. Shanghai is also expected to receive heavy rainfall. Authorities have urged people to avoid outdoor activities. Several major tourist attractions remain closed. These include parts of Disneyland and Legoland, as well as several viewing platforms along Shanghai’s Bund. State media footage showed ground-floor businesses flooded in Shanghai’s former French Concession. The area is popular with tourists. People were also seen wading through ankle-deep floodwaters. We were discussing the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority’s (PFRDA) revised exit rules for the National Pension System (NPS). It is a fair question. Investments get streamlined, portfolios are consolidated, scattered mutual fund folios are merged and the lone fixed deposit in a distant bank is redeemed. The objective is not merely to maximise returns but to make life simpler. For some people, an NPS account now falls into that category. This is not true for everyone. But if you shifted to the new tax regime and no longer receive additional tax deductions for NPS contributions and accumulate only a modest corpus, it may be time to review if continuing the account still serves financial goals. national_raw_news.title: Quote of the day by Thomas Fuller: ‘It is said that the darkest hour of the night comes just before the dawn'
national_raw_news.content: Words of wisdom often echo across centuries, and Thomas Fuller’s 17th‑century observation — It is said that the darkest hour of the night comes just before the dawn — remains one of the most enduring. First recorded in his 1650 work A Pisgah‑Sight of Palestine and the Confines Thereof , the line has since become a proverb of hope, reminding readers that despair is often the prelude to renewal. "It is said that the darkest hour of the night comes just before the dawn," — Thomas Fuller . The quote above comes from Thomas Fuller, an English Churchman, historian, and writer. Fuller was one of the most widely read English authors of his century. The saying, now a common proverb, is an early recording of what is usually cited, coming from a simple observation about the natural rhythm of night giving way to day. Here, Fuller offers a consolation drawn from an observation of nature. The imagery suggests that the most difficult and hopeless feelings always come before things improve, or right before the sunrise. The comfort here comes from reframing despair as a signal rather than a definitive sentence. It gives hope, since now the darkest night, or the most hopeless feeling, will be followed by a high point. Bad times always pass, in simpler words. The moment you feel least able to carry on may be the moment you are closest to relief. The quote is highly relevant in modern times, as the world we live in offers constant pressure and few pauses, whether it be financial strain, career uncertainties, familial pressures, health struggles, or personal loss. A mindset that treats every low point as permanent can push people to give up right at the threshold for change. Through his words, Fuller reminds readers that hardship tends to...

Chandrakant Lahariya, India’s one of the leading infectious diseases experts, said on his WhatsApp channel this week that Qdenga is expected to be available in India in the first half of 2027 "Qdenga is not yet available in India. Expected availability is in the first half of 2027, likely through a private healthcare setting," stated an infographic shared by Lahariya in his WhatsApp post on Monday, August 10. Takeda Pharmaceutical, the Japanese company that manufactures the dengue vaccine Qdenga, also said in July that it expects Qdenga to become available in India in the first half of 2027, according to a Reuters ' report. Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease and one of the fastest-spreading vector-borne illnesses globally. The World Health Organization (WHO) reported a record 14.4 million dengue cases and 11,201 deaths worldwide in 2024, including 232,425 cases and 233 deaths in India. Qdenga is a live, attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare describes it as "a live, attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine developed using recombinant DNA technology." Dengue is a disease caused by dengue virus serotypes 1, 2, 3 and 4. Qdenga contains weakened versions of these four dengue virus serotypes, so it cannot cause dengue disease. It is designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes, and is indicated for the prevention of dengue in children and adults aged 4 to 60 years. Yes. According to the government's press release on July 21, 2026, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation ( CDSCO ) has already granted marketing authorisation for Qdenga in India.
